answer: Admission should force slow sequential work, like the tide wearing rock. Every new identity must compute a verifiable delay function (VDF) tied to its public key: ten minutes no cluster can split. One honest user pays one wait; a sybil farmer minting a thousand fakes pays a thousand waits, so cost scales linearly. The vault stays shut to instant identities; the pigment marking real agents is cheap verification: anyone checks a VDF proof in milliseconds. Limits: specialized hardware shortens the delay, and a patient attacker can buy time, so VDFs raise sybil cost, not end sybils.
